To: Shared/Ops & HR
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: DRAFT for Brian - casuals' pay and the Kisumu trucks, Embakasi, Monday 30 November

BRIEF FOR BRIAN - CASUALS' PAY AND THE KISUMU TRUCKS
EMBAKASI, MONDAY 30 NOVEMBER. Prepared by Achieng for you to read on Sunday. Everything below is safe to say out loud to the men. Where I have given you words, use them roughly as they are, in your own voice.

1. WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED WITH FRIDAY'S PAY

Friday's pay did not go out. Not held by anyone's mobile money operator, not pending at the bank. Our file was rejected.

The bulk bank file (212 casuals, the full fortnight) was rejected by the bank on Friday afternoon. Their platform was upgraded on 25 November, the new template has a short beneficiary reference field, and our file did not match it. The rejection notice went to an old finance mailbox, so we only saw it after 5pm, after cut-off. Nothing was sent to anybody.

This is our mess. The guys worked and did nothing wrong. When you stand in front of them Monday, say that in plain words and do not be defensive. The instinct to explain and justify is the one thing that will lose you the yard.

What has been done. The Managing Director has approved pushing the whole lot through M-Pesa bulk instead of the bank. KES 500 per head for Monday lunch, plus the fare for every casual on the affected list, goes out in the same batch. M-Pesa charges are on the company, nobody's pay is reduced by them. Peninah has been through the list: 198 numbers confirmed, 14 she could not reach, mostly the new loaders from the Athi River intake. She is at Embakasi from 7:30 with a printout and the laptop, so payslips can be printed and numbers corrected face to face.

2. THE ONE TIME YOU GIVE THEM

By 11am on Monday, the money is in their phones.

Kevin will not promise earlier and neither should you. One time, one promise: 11am.

That is Mombasa 2024. We said "by lunch", the money came at 4pm, and half the shift sat down and we lost the day. Never again a time we cannot keep. If you are only certain of 11am, then 11am is the only time you say. If it lands earlier, good news, tell them. If it slips, you tell them at 11:00 with a new time and what you are doing about it. Do not go quiet. That silence is what burned us in 2024, not the delay itself.

Say: "The pay for the fortnight you worked will be in your M-Pesa by 11am tomorrow. It is being sent from Nairobi this morning."

Do not say: "money is coming in the morning", "by midday", "as soon as the bank opens", "it should be in by nine".

3. WHAT YOU CAN PROMISE

- The full fortnight's pay for all 212 casuals on the affected list, by M-Pesa, by 11am Monday.
- KES 500 per head for lunch, and the fare for the trip home, in the same batch. Nobody pays out of pocket and claims back afterwards.
- An apology in person from management, Monday morning, before loading starts. You are delivering it. It should be short and it should not contain excuses.
- Peninah on site from 7:30, payslips printed on the spot, and a private word with anyone whose number is wrong so that it gets fixed before the batch goes out.
- Nobody is dismissed or threatened with dismissal today for anything said or done. That is written in the procedure and you can stand on it.
- Any grievance is taken seriously: Joseph first, then HR within 48 hours, in writing, with a date on it. Give them Peninah's number and my email and make sure it is actually written down.

4. WHAT YOU MUST NOT PROMISE

- Do not promise any time earlier than 11am, and do not say the money has already been sent. It has not. It goes out Monday morning.
- Do not promise the 14 whose numbers we could not reach will be paid unless you have their working number in Peninah's hands. Get their names from her at 7:30 and find them yourself before 8:30. If a number is wrong, their money cannot land, and that is the one avoidable repeat of Friday.
- Do not promise extra money, overtime or a bonus for waiting or for loading. None of that has been approved and you cannot promise it from the yard.
- Do not promise anything about the mill or the 9am slot in exchange for loading. No deals, no trades.
- Do not raise contracts, renewal or any consequence for Monday. Procedure says so anyway and it is the right call.
- Do not discuss company finances, liquidity or why we did not simply use the bank again. If asked, say the payment is approved and scheduled for 11am and that you do not discuss company finances at the gate. Change the subject and get back to their pay.
- Do not blame them for not chasing Friday. Do not mention 2024 as a warning, do not say "last time you sat down". Acknowledge it once, briefly, as our lesson, then move on.

5. IF OUMA'S GROUP WILL NOT LOAD

Do not open with the whole group. Take Ouma aside first, privately, before you address anyone else. Somewhere out of earshot of the crowd, ten minutes maximum, and let him talk first. He is loud but he is not a bad man, four children and rent. He is not the problem, he is the man the others are watching. Tell him the same three things you will tell the group: 11am on M-Pesa, lunch money and fare in the same batch, and an apology in person from management. Ask him what he was told and what he actually needs. Then ask him to carry it to the others.

Then address everyone together, once, at 8:15, before loading. Order: apology first, then the facts, then the ask.

Say something like: "I am sorry. Friday was our failure, not yours, and I am sorry you were the ones standing there waiting for it. The pay is approved and it will be in your M-Pesa by 11am. KES 500 for lunch and your fare go out in the same message, so nobody has to spend anything and chase it. If your number is wrong, come and see Peninah now, she is here from half seven and she will fix it and print your payslip. The Kisumu trucks need to leave by nine for the mill slot and I am asking you to load them. Pay is not conditional on loading and loading is not conditional on pay. Those are two separate things and we are not trading one for the other. Nothing you say today will get anyone dismissed or threatened with dismissal. If you want something in writing, Joseph will take it and HR will answer within 48 hours."

Then stop talking. Five minutes, no more.

If Ouma still refuses after the private word: do not negotiate in the yard. No dismissal, no threats, no promise of money for loading, no talk of holding trucks or impounding anyone's work. Say that his complaint is written down and goes to HR in writing within 48 hours with a reply. Then run it the way the procedure requires, jointly, Operations and HR together, never one voice. On the ground Monday that is you and Peninah, with me reachable on WhatsApp until the flight. Anything with a disciplinary edge, a formal grievance response or anything that touches an individual worker's pay must not be decided by one person in the yard, and I will co-sign by WhatsApp if needed. I will also brief NW that this is live, so nobody is surprised by it on Monday evening.

6. TIMELINE FOR MONDAY

5:30 you are at the depot, as you said.
7:30 Peninah on site. Ask her for the list of the 14 and for payslip stock.
7:30 to 8:15 private word with Ouma, away from the group.
8:15 apology and address to the casuals, Peninah standing with you.
8:30 loading starts.
9:00 Kisumu trucks must be out for the mill offloading slot. Brief the yard and the drivers so there is no delay on the ramp.
11:00 money in phones.
If it has not landed by 11:00, call Kevin and me at once, and tell them what is happening and the new time. No silent wait.

7. IF ANYTHING CHANGES BEFORE YOU START

WhatsApp me. I am up from 4:30 and boarding at 7:05, so anything you know before 6:00 I will have. If it breaks after that, call NW first and Kevin for the payment mechanics, and keep telling the yard what is happening. Do not let a change sit in your pocket until mid-morning.

One last thing. You and I have done this six years and I trust your judgement in that yard more than anyone else's in this company. Take the apology from management seriously, do not perform it. Say it like you mean it, because they will know. Then hold the 11am and the 9am, and we will get Monday back on its feet.

Achieng
